_: Golden for the us.srp-e27 preset — D2 §9 1 and 4, D9 §3. SRP is the 30-minute demand interval and the tiered $/kW; the eligibility window is what makes an 8 kW evening free.

sources.grammar: HLD §8's US row: SRP `(30, ...)` — a 30-minute demand interval, the rest as APS. D2 §9 4 names SRP's on-peak window as the eligibility case.
sources.interval_and_hours: srpnet.com E-27 material as reported 2026-09-19: summer weekdays use a 2pm-8pm on-peak window and "the demand charge is based on your highest average kW reading across a fixed 30-minute interval during on-peak hours in the billing month".
sources.tiers: ASSUMED. $11.90/kW for the first 3 kW, $19.97/kW for the next 7 kW and $36.05/kW above 10 kW, per secondary reporting of the 2026 E-27 worksheet; SRP's own price sheet was not read inside this WP's lookup budget. The three-band shape is the load-bearing part and is why this preset is `Tiers` and not `Linear`.
sources.season: ASSUMED, and a grammar limit: SRP's winter season (November-April) has its own on-peak hours (05:00-09:00 and 17:00-21:00) and its own lower tiers, and `PeakTariff` carries one `eligible` and one `pricing` per version. This preset covers the summer season, May-October. A winter month therefore has no capacity component and the site steers on price alone (HLD §3). See the preset's `assumed`.
sources.month: Constructed, not measured: July 2026, two eligible half-hours and two that must be invisible.
sources.metric_kw: A 30-minute window's kW is twice its kWh: 1.55 kWh -> 3.10 kW and 3.10 kWh -> 6.20 kW. per_day = all with per_period = max takes the higher, 6.20 kW.
sources.not_metric_kw: 8.00 kW — the 4.00 kWh half-hour at 21:00 on 2026-07-08, off-peak. The 7.00 kW half-hour on Saturday 2026-07-11 is invisible too.
sources.fee: Marginal integration over the bands (D2 §5.3): the first 3.00 kW at 11.90 = 35.70, the next 3.20 kW (3.00 to 6.20) at 19.97 = 63.904, and nothing in the third band. 35.70 + 63.904 = 99.604 USD for the month.
sources.temporary_reduction: SRP applied a temporary $0.0038/kWh reduction to the May-October 2026 billing cycles; it is an energy adjustment, not a demand one, so it does not appear here.

eligibility.why: December is outside the summer season this version covers

eligible_windows.why: 14:00-20:00 in half hours is twelve windows
